narrative:
The model estimates a 23% chance that you will fail the final year. That does not mean failure is certain; it means the risk is high enough, under this school’s remedial rule, that extra courses are required now.

The strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure is that you do not intend to pursue higher education. This stands out because every student who passed in the comparison group wanted to continue to higher education. The second most important factor works in your favor: your reason for choosing the school was its reputation, which pushed toward passing; about 29% of passing students chose it for the same reason. The third most important factor also works in your favor: you have no past class failures, matching the passing group’s average of zero.

Even with those positives, your weekly study time is under two hours, while most passing students study two to five hours. Next, speak with a counselor about whether higher education or another clear post-school goal fits you, build a weekly study routine of at least two to five hours, and ask family or school staff for regular academic support. Your zero absences and clean failure record are strengths to protect.
